answer: Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 23 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. Because the umber cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the sable ledger, the relic audit exposes how much each key had accrued when it was cut. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. The deposit is 38 dollars a seat. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
